messages:
maria: quick sketch — want to prototype a synth generator that mixes a spiketrain (microbursts) on top of a low-rate poisson baseline, but with controlled KV-cache priming and explicit kernel-stress windows so we can validate kernel selection + batching heuristics apples-to-apples.

sam: sounds good. can you share a minimal config example?

maria: here's the idea config (pseudo):
```
seed: 42
baseline: { qps: 50, dist: poisson }
spiketrain: { pattern: 'burst', bursts_per_min: 6, burst_qps: [800, 1200], duration_ms: 200 }
warmup: [ {type: 'kv-prime', duration_s: 30, seq_len: 64, fanout: 8} ]
stress_windows: [ {start_s: 60, duration_s: 15, force_model_variant: 'float16', force_kernel: 'jit_opt'}, ... ]
session_affinity: true
record: [latency_hist, kernel_trace, batch_util, kv_hits]
```

alex: nice. two notes: 1) to validate kernel selection we should tag requests with request_meta: {seq_len, prompt_template, model_hint} so traces can be grouped. 2) for apples-to-apples, freeze model binary + env flags (no dynamic quantization toggles).

kevin: for batching heuristics test, add a dynamic target batch size schedule: start at 8, ramp to 64 during spikes, and include an artificial backoff when p95>200ms. we want to see kernel-switch churn when batch size jumps.

maria: agreed. also important: KV warmup needs both cold and warm experiments. plan: run 3x phases per job: cold (no KV), warm-prime (run warmup snippet), steady-state (baseline+spikes). compare p50/p95/p99 and kernel selection counts.

perf-bot: perf-capture started: trace_id=trc-2026-03-18-250123, collecting kernel_trace, batch_metrics, kv_stats.

sam: replay harness question — if we replay real traffic vs synth, session affinity can re-use KV state incorrectly. we should reset KV per-run or provide deterministic session ids.

alex: exactly. make session ids deterministic from seed: session_id = sha1(seed + user_idx) so KV hits are reproducible across runs.

kevin: metrics we should ingest: tokens/s, avg_batch_size, batch_fill_percent, kernel_switch_rate, kv_hit_ratio, tail_latency_by_seq_len. plot as time-series with event markers for stress windows.

maria: for kernel traces capture the kernel name and reason for selection, e.g.
```
[KERNEL_TRACE] timestamp=2501234680 kernel="fused_attention_v2" reason="seq_len>512 and quantized=false"
[KERNEL_TRACE] timestamp=2501234712 kernel="matmul_fast_q8" reason="quantized=true and batch_size>=32"
```
this helps correlate when the runtime flips kernels during a burst.

sam: how long should runs be? i'm thinking 10m per seed to get enough long-tail samples, run 5 seeds each.

maria: 10m x 5 seeds sounds right. keep infra constant (same instance types) and pin model/weights. disable any autoscaling that might mask perf.

alex: regression detection: run baseline before changes, then run after change with same seeds and config. compute per-query delta and an aggregated KS test on latency distributions per seq_len bucket. flag if p99 increases >5% and kernel_switch_rate increases >10%.

kevin: also capture raw grpc/http traces for a few samples so we can repro locally. small sample dump of inputs + kv_state snapshot.

maria: action items: 1) sam — wire deterministic session ids into replay harness, 2) kevin — add batch-size schedule control and metrics hooks, 3) alex — add kernel_trace exporter and KS regression check, 4) i'll produce the initial job spec and seed configs. we'll run an end-to-end tomorrow morning and tag perf-bot. :coffee:

sam: ack.

alex: ack.

kevin: ack — will prototype batch schedule today.
